title: Kashmir Shaivism opening (the Shiva Sutras)
hook: a thread of the Shiva Sutras says wonder marks the stages of yoga, and the week ends on astonishment

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kashmir Shaivism opening gave us its second thread: knowledge is bondage, the small knowing that says I am only this. Did you catch an I'm just, and add and much more? Day one thousand one hundred forty-one.

A toddler sees a dog. Not for the first time, not even close, and still the whole body lights up: the pointing finger, the gasp, the word shouted at the whole street. Dog! Somewhere along the way, grown-ups stop gasping at dogs. The Shiva Sutras, a book of very short, very serious lines about the self and Shiva, has a thread that sounds like it was written by that toddler. Vismayo yogabhumikah. Wonder marks the stages of yoga. Today we end the week on astonishment, still inside the opening of Kashmir Shaivism.
screen: `A TODDLER SEES A DOG.` → `VISMAYO YOGABHUMIKAH.` → `WONDER MARKS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Vismaya is wonder, astonishment, the wide-eyed surprise of seeing something as if for the first time. And yogabhumikah: the grounds, the levels, the stages of yoga. Put them together and the thread says that in this path, wonder is how you can tell you're on the way. Not a fixed posture, not a list of achievements. Amazement. Why would that be? Go back to the first two threads. Consciousness is the self. And knowing binds: the small sense of I am only this. Commentators in the tradition describe the yogi who starts to see through that small picture. Every time the wider self shows up, the response is astonishment. Not pride. Not I've earned this. Something more like: oh. This was here the whole time? Wonder is what recognition feels like from the inside. So here's the week, in a line. We watched Vishnu offer a lotus at every name, and nearly his eye. We met Shiva the blue-throated, holding poison, and Kapardin, the wild one a village asked for help. We gathered the names as Mahadeva, through a boy who wanted milk. Then the book changed. A rock turned over in Kashmir. Consciousness is the self. Knowing binds. And now: wonder marks the way. Two very different books, and the week ends on a small word that fits both: oh.
screen: `VISMAYA: WONDER, ASTONISHMENT.` · `WONDER MARKS THE STAGES OF YOGA.` · `RECOGNITION FEELS LIKE OH.` · `THIS WEEK: NAMES, THEN THREADS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look at one ordinary thing as if it's the first time. Sit, and let the breath settle. Then choose something right in front of you: your hand, a cup, the light on a wall. Look at it the way the toddler looks at the dog. Its color. Its edges. The fact that it's here at all. When the mind says, it's just a cup, let that pass and look again. Then turn the same wonder inward, on the plain fact that you're aware of anything. If you pray, you can let that wonder be your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Kashmir Shaivism opening. A thread from the Shiva Sutras: vismayo yogabhumikah, wonder marks the stages of yoga. Astonishment is what recognition feels like.
Your line: Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras. Today, let one ordinary thing surprise you, and stay with the surprise for one breath longer than usual. Day one thousand one hundred forty-one.

what a scholar hears: Shiva Sutra 1.12, vismayo yogabhumikah, which commentators tie to the yogi's delight in recognizing the self.
